html:
The Bombay Stock Exchange is the stock market of Mumbai, formed in 1875 as the Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association. It is the oldest stock exchange in Asia.

It grew out of informal trading. From the 1850s a handful of brokers met under a banyan tree near the Town Hall to deal in shares. During the American Civil War, when cotton from the American South was cut off, Bombay's cotton exports boomed and a wild share mania followed, then a crash in 1865. Brokers wanted rules, and in 1875 they formed the association, led by men such as Premchand Roychand. They later settled on what is now Dalal Street.

It listed the firms that built modern Indian industry, among them the Tata companies. After independence it was given legal recognition in 1957. Its Sensex index, begun in 1986, became the country's best known measure of the economy.

After economic liberalisation in 1991 and a stock scam in 1992, India set up a new rival, the National Stock Exchange, and both moved to screen trading. Pakistan's Karachi Stock Exchange opened in 1947.
sum: The Bombay Stock Exchange is the stock market of Mumbai, formed in 1875 as the Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association. It is the oldest stock exchange in Asia.
